comments.body:
One unrelated test failed in this ticket's full-suite run and did NOT reproduce. Recording it as an open question rather than a diagnosis.

The failure: tests/interfaces/lifecycle/test_ref_coherence.py::test_attested_claim_gate_ignores_unrelated_committed_change — 'rebar._errors.RebarError: rebar create failed (exit 1): Error: git commit f…' (truncated; the suite ran under -q so the traceback is lost). 1 failed, 12859 passed.

What I checked:
- Isolated re-run: passed in 64s.
- Reproduction sweep: three consecutive runs of tests/interfaces/lifecycle/ at -n 3 --dist worksteal, 448 tests each, ALL PASSED (169s, 162s, 265s). Not reproduced in ~1344 test executions.
- My first hypothesis was store-lock contention from the concurrent session that held the tracker flock for 100s+ stretches all afternoon. Reading the test REFUTES that: _repo() builds a repo under tmp_path and monkeypatches REBAR_ROOT to it, so it never touches the shared tracker. I discarded the hypothesis rather than reporting it.

What I did NOT conclude: a root cause. The git-commit failure inside an isolated temp repo has no explanation I can support with evidence, and the traceback that would have supplied one was discarded by -q.

Why it is not attributable to this change: this diff is CONTRIBUTING.md, AGENTS.md, src/rebar/_guides/passing-code-review.md, and one new test module. None is reachable from attest.claim_gate_check or the store write path.

Left as an open question, not filed as a bug: a single unreproduced failure with no traceback does not meet the bar for a bug ticket that someone else would have to act on, and filing it would be indistinguishable from noise. If it recurs on CI, the run log will have the traceback under CI's own verbosity and it should be filed then, with this comment as the first datapoint.

## Context / Problem
Operator directive (verbatim, 2026-08-13): 'Update our contribution flow to note that Gerrit changes that have known issues like these should be marked as "work in progress" to avoid erroneous submission.'

The incident it encodes: during a fleet pause, change 1727's revision f34549d099 carried five known review defects (including a silent compaction-suppression bug). The hold was recorded in ticket comments and a session log — and a peer session, correctly following the standing "both votes +1 => Submit" rule, submitted it anyway (merged as d2dea317ec, fixed forward by 8fd5166a7b). This session watched the second-order cost directly: d2dea317ec also pushed `src/rebar/_config_schema.py` to 808 lines over the locked 800-LOC cap, turning main red and costing change 1731 a `Verified -1` it had nothing to do with.

The lesson is a mechanism gap, not a discipline gap. A hold recorded in a ticket or a session log is invisible to the submitter; nothing in the contribution flow tells an author how to make a hold ENFORCEABLE. Gerrit already has that mechanism — a change in Work In Progress state cannot be submitted — and none of our contribution docs mention it.

## Approach
One authoritative wording in CONTRIBUTING.md §2d (the iterate-and-re-push step, where an author is by definition holding a change with known findings); the other two surfaces point at it.

1. **CONTRIBUTING.md §2d** — after the amend/re-push recipe, add the rule: when a pushed change has known unresolved issues — review findings still being folded in, a defect found after pushing, or any deliberate hold — mark it WIP immediately. Give both forms, because which one applies depends on whether the change exists yet: `git push gerrit HEAD:refs/for/main%wip` at push time, and `POST /a/changes/<n>/wip` (or the Gerrit UI's "Mark as work in progress") for a change already up. Unmark with `%ready` / `POST /a/changes/<n>/ready` once resolved. State the rationale in one sentence: ticket comments and session logs are advisory and invisible to a submitter, while WIP is the only hold every submitter — human, bot, or another agent session — is structurally forced to respect. Cite the 1727 incident in one clause as the worked example.
2. **The packaged code-review guide** — `src/rebar/_guides/passing-code-review.md`, surfaced by `rebar explain review`, has an iterate-on-findings paragraph ("Iterate by **amending the same commit**…"). Mirror the rule there in two sentences with both spellings, pointing at CONTRIBUTING.md §2d for the full text. This guide is the on-ramp an agent reads before pushing, so the rule has to be reachable without opening CONTRIBUTING.md.
3. **AGENTS.md** — one line in the existing Git-workflow bullet list, in that list's style, pointing at CONTRIBUTING.md §2d.
4. **Regenerate the guide pin manifest, don't hand-edit** — `src/rebar/_guides/criterion-pins.json` is GENERATED (`python -m rebar.llm.plan_review.guide_parity regenerate`) from digests of the criteria cited by the guides, and `tests/unit/test_generated_surface_markers.py` fails if the committed file differs. The edit cites no criterion, so the expected outcome is NO diff; run the regenerate and commit whatever it produces rather than assuming.

**Deliberately not done.** No tooling, hook, or automation to apply WIP — the directive is a documentation change, and an auto-WIP heuristic would fight the normal flow. No change to the submit rule itself: "both votes +1 and no unresolved comments" stays exactly as it is, because WIP is an additional gate on top of it, not a replacement for it.

## Scope
- `CONTRIBUTING.md` — §2d gains the WIP rule (the authoritative wording).
- `src/rebar/_guides/passing-code-review.md` — mirrored two sentences in the iterate section.
- `AGENTS.md` — one pointer line in the Git-workflow list.
- `src/rebar/_guides/criterion-pins.json` — regenerated (expected: unchanged).
- `tests/unit/test_wip_hold_guidance.py` — new; pins the rule across all three surfaces.

## Testing
The testable behavior is that the rule is present and reachable on every surface an author or agent actually reads, so a future edit cannot quietly drop it from one of the three.
- **Happy path:** a new `tests/unit/test_wip_hold_guidance.py` asserts CONTRIBUTING.md §2d carries both spellings (`%wip` and the `/wip` REST endpoint), the unmark path (`%ready` / `/ready`), and the rationale clause; that `src/rebar/_guides/passing-code-review.md` carries the mirrored rule; and that AGENTS.md carries the pointer.
- **Reachability, not just presence:** the same module asserts the rule is reachable through the packaged surface by loading the guide the way `rebar explain review` does (`rebar.llm.plan_review.registry`'s `review -> passing-code-review.md` mapping) rather than by reading the file path directly — a file-path-only assertion would still pass if the guide stopped being packaged.
- **Failure path:** verified by deleting the `%wip` sentence from CONTRIBUTING.md locally and confirming the suite goes red before restoring it.
- **Generator no-diff:** `python -m rebar.llm.plan_review.guide_parity regenerate` leaves the tree clean, and `tests/unit/test_generated_surface_markers.py` passes.
- **Gates:** `make lint`, `make typecheck`, the `check_*` gates, and the CI unit selection.

## Acceptance Criteria
- [ ] `CONTRIBUTING.md` §2d documents the WIP hold with BOTH the push-time `%wip` form and the REST toggle, names the unmark path, and states the rationale that comments and tickets are advisory while WIP is enforceable.
- [ ] `rebar explain review` surfaces the same rule — asserted by loading the guide through the packaged registry mapping, not by reading the file path — and the guide-pin manifest is regenerated with no hand edits.
- [ ] `AGENTS.md` carries a one-line pointer in the Git-workflow list, restating no CONTRIBUTING text.
- [ ] `tests/unit/test_wip_hold_guidance.py` passes, and the deletion check in Testing confirms it fails when the rule is removed.
- [ ] `make lint`, `make typecheck`, and the CI unit selection are green.
